verses.1: In the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar’s reign, during which Pontius Pilate ruled over Judea, and Herodian ruled over Galilee. Also, Philip, the brother of Tiberius, ruled over Ituraea. And Trachonitis also came under his rule. Additionally, Lysanias of Abilene also ruled during that time.
verses.2: Upon the archbishop Hanna and Kaifah, there came a miracle from God upon John Zacharias, son of Zachariah, in the wilderness.
verses.3: And he went to every corner of the Jordan River, proclaiming the message of repentance for sin.
verses.4: As it is written in the book of the words of the prophet Esaias: “The voice of a shepherd in the wilderness.” Prepare the path for the Lord, and make his steps easy to follow.
verses.5: All mountains and hills will be leveled off. The steep slopes will become flat, and the difficult terrain will become easy to traverse.
verses.6: And all flesh sees the salvation of the Lord.
verses.7: He said to those who were leading the crowd, “Let them be baptized by him. As for the offspring of the wicked, who can tell you that you should flee from the impending wrath?”
verses.8: So, you have produced fruits worthy of repentance. But do not begin to speak among yourselves about this. We have Abraham as our father. I tell you that God can indeed create sons from these stones for Abraham.
verses.9: Also, the branches of the trees are cut off. Every tree that doesn’t produce any good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
verses.10: And the crowd, who were around him, said to him, “What shall we do?”
verses.11: And he replied to them, “He who has two bags will give to those who don’t have any. And he who has ointments will do the same.”
verses.12: And we also came to be baptized. Then we said to him, “Teacher, what should we do?”
verses.13: And he said to them, “Do not ask anything more from those who have been appointed as your rulers.”
verses.14: And those who were with him also asked him, “What shall we do?” He replied to them, “Do not say anything or reveal anything. Be obedient to your leaders.”
verses.15: Assuming that the people were thinking about this, and that all of them were pondering in their hearts about John the Baptist. Whether he really was the Christ or not…
verses.16: He replied, “All of you are John the Baptist. I alone baptize you with water. But my Lord will come after me; I am not worthy to carry his cross. He himself will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.”
verses.17: And that substance, when it is mixed with water in his hands, will dissolve the dirt on his hands and bring the dirt into its proper place. But that bitter substance can be destroyed by burning it with calcium oxide.
verses.18: So, many other things were also commanded by God to be done.
verses.19: And Heroides, the tetrarch, who was in charge of everything related to his brother’s wife and all the evil deeds that Heroides had committed.
verses.20: This also was added to all of them. As a result, John was put in prison.
verses.21: And during the baptism, all the people were baptized as well. When Jesus was baptized and prayed, heaven opened for him.
verses.22: And the holy spirit would descend upon him in the form of a dove; also, a voice would come from heaven. You are indeed my beloved son, whom I cherish greatly.
verses.23: And Jesus himself began his life at the age of thirty. He was considered to be the son of Eli.
